what: Two corruption campaigns against the dependent-substream path, which the earlier ones could not reach because neither of their streams has a dependent substream
why: `program.rs` is the largest and newest code on this branch and the dependent `bsi` it parses had never executed on real material. `frame.rs` seeks the audio frame header to `bsi.end_bit`, so one bit wrong in that parse gives a garbage frame rather than a slightly wrong one -- which is the risk phase 1 existed to retire
material: 400 frame groups of the 1917 Dolby Digital Plus track: an AC-3 core at acmod 7 + LFE and an E-AC-3 dependent at acmod 5 with chanmap 0x1a00, 363 dependent frames

campaign_1_single_bit_anywhere.what_it_shows: no panic, no silent success, exit 7 on all 150 from all three arms -- the programme decode, the `--core-only` decode and `verify` agree site for site
campaign_1_single_bit_anywhere.what_it_does_not_show: anything about the parser. Every single-bit error lands under the frame CRC and is caught before any syntax is read: 136 of the 150 report CRC failures and the other 14 report decode errors

campaign_2_inside_the_dependent_header_w.range: bits 40 to 79 of a dependent frame, which is where `bsi` ends according to `eac3-blocks`. Past it are the audio blocks, where every bit pattern is legal: a flip there changes the audio without making the stream malformed, so no decoder can report it and counting those would measure nothing
campaign_2_inside_the_dependent_header_w.result: 0 panics. 159 of 200 reported and exited 7. The other 41 said nothing -- and in every one of those the decoded audio is byte-identical to the clean decode, on both the programme path and `--core-only`, so the silence is correct
campaign_2_inside_the_dependent_header_w.what_the_silent_bits_are: `dialnorm` at 45 to 49, `compre`/`compr` from 50, and the information flags after the channel map -- fields that a decoder may read and that do not reach the samples of this programme
campaign_2_inside_the_dependent_header_w.what_the_reported_ones_say: decode errors where the flip breaks the syntax, and eight trials where the new channel-map validation names the fault directly: "the channel map names ...". That path had never run on any input before this branch

the_gate: silent corrupted output, 0 of 350 across both campaigns; panics, 0. The distinction that makes the second number mean something is between saying nothing about a change that did not reach the audio, which is correct, and saying nothing while the audio moves, which is the failure. The tool counts them separately
